
            writer.Write(MAGIC4);
            writer.Write(Data.Header!.Format.Id.ToByteArray());
            // VPKSTUFF PATCH: emit LZ4-compressed body so the output matches the
            // shape Valve's resourcecompiler produces. CS2's material loader is
            // strict — uncompressed vmat_c bytes are rejected — but the KV3
            // reader at BinaryKV3.cs:317 already handles compressionMethod=1
            // natively, so this is purely a writer-side change.
            // IMPORTANT: Only use LZ4 (method 1) when there are no binary blobs.
            // When binary blobs are present (e.g. MDAT in vmdl_c with meshlet data),
            // the reader expects blobs to be compressed with the same method — but we
            // only LZ4 the body, not the blobs. Use method 0 (uncompressed) for those
            // blocks; CS2 model loader accepts uncompressed KV3, only vmat_c is strict.
            // See docs/SKINS_TODO.md "Option 2 — Phase B/C" + PATCHES.md.
            var useLz4 = context.BinaryBlobLengths.Count == 0;
            writer.Write(useLz4 ? 1 : 0); // compressionMethod: 1=LZ4, 0=uncompressed
            writer.Write((ushort)0); // compressionDictionaryId
            writer.Write(useLz4 ? (ushort)16384 : (ushort)0); // compressionFrameSize
            writer.Write((int)context.Bytes1.Length);
            writer.Write((int)context.Bytes4.Length / 4);
            writer.Write((int)context.Bytes8.Length / 8);
